name: חָנוּן
summary: The passive participle of חָנַן, “one shown favour”. Borne by Hanun son of Nahash, king of Ammon, to whom David sent to show חֶסֶד at his father's death; Hanun, counselled that they were spies, shaved half their beards and cut their garments, and brought war on Ammon (2Sa 10:1–4; 1Ch 19:2–6); and in the return by Hanun who with the people of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, who repaired another section (Neh 3:13, 30).

evidence.note: “Hanun his son reigned in his place.”
“I will show חֶסֶד to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed חֶסֶד to me.”
“Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate.”
The verb's passive, “let favour be shown (יֻחַן) to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness”.

note: Takes h.dz.ah (11 tokens). The form is the qal passive participle (qātûl), “favoured”; scripture does not explain it.
